pages.title: emb — no route here
pages.description: This address is not served by this site. The landing page and the documentation are one link away.

pages.title: emb — demos: the atlas — a corpus laid out by meaning
pages.description: 2 782 passages from one author's collected works, drawn as they sit in the model's space: named regions, a query that lands among its neighbours, and an order switch that separates meaning from chronology.
pages.social_description: The corpus drawn by meaning: named regions, a live query landing among its neighbours, and the space between two passages.

pages.title: emb — demos: the batch — one call, many texts
pages.description: Six passages embedded two ways against the same server: six separate EMB calls, then one call carrying all six. The server's own timings show what batching buys.
pages.social_description: Six texts, two ways: six round trips versus one. Measured on the server, drawn to scale.

pages.title: emb — demos: the cache — the second call is already answered
pages.description: The same passage embedded twice. The first call fills emb's cache; the second is a hit, and the server's own counters show it.
pages.social_description: Ask once, ask again: emb memoizes the vector, and the second answer is a lookup instead of a model pass.

pages.title: emb — demos: the perception — depth says where, DINOv3 says what
pages.description: One photograph, two calls: a depth model puts every pixel in space and DINOv3 answers with a vector per patch. The result is one indexed surface with five readings — textured, wireframe, camera-space normals, depth contours, dense cloud — plus a probe that finds any part again in the other five photographs.
pages.social_description: Depth says where. DINOv3 says what. One reconstructed surface you can turn, wireframe, shade by normal, contour by depth, cut in half and search — from two live calls.

pages.title: emb — demos: the zone — a DNS name is a sentence, a TXT record is the answer
pages.description: dns.emb.is, a DNS zone where every name is a sentence: the query, the ranked emoji, and the same answer printed twice — the escaped TXT data a resolver hands back and the glyph it stands for.
pages.social_description: Semantic retrieval over DNS: every name under dns.emb.is is a query, and the reply is one TXT record per ranked emoji.

pages.title: emb — demos: the model is a function — one primitive, four answers
pages.description: The same passage through the raw command and two preloaded Lua presets: bytes, a typed vector, a similarity and a label. The server runs scripts it preloaded; raw Lua stays refused.
pages.social_description: One primitive, four answers: raw bytes, a typed vector, a similarity and a label from the same server.

pages.title: emb — demos: the graph — a similarity graph built by a script
pages.description: Eight passages from the corpus, embedded in one batch and linked to their nearest neighbours by a Lua script on the server. A directed graph of the space, computed next to the model.
pages.social_description: The scripting layer computes an N-by-N similarity graph next to the model and returns edges, not a matrix. Drawn as a directed graph.

pages.title: emb — demos: the image — a photo, matched to words
pages.description: Drop an image on the sandbox and watch a vision model place it in the same space as text: eight candidate labels, scored live, in one shared graph.
pages.social_description: One model, two modalities: an image and eight labels scored in the same space, live on the sandbox.

pages.title: emb — the demos gallery: vectors, similarity, search, the atlas, the image, the parts, the graph, the decision, the zone, the medium
pages.description: Fifteen small demonstrations run against a real embeddings server and a real vector index: what a vector is, why it retrieves by meaning, why two models produce two incomparable spaces, what a call costs, what a script can compute — and decide — beside the model, how a DNS zone asks the same model a question, how a fingerprint names a recording while an embedding only describes it, and how one image becomes a grid of vectors whose parts match by meaning.
pages.social_description: A gallery of fifteen demos that embed real text, images and media and search a real index, over one author's public-domain corpus.

pages.title: emb — the decision engine: typed questions, one forward pass
pages.description: Laya is a decision model. A state goes in; a tree of typed questions — choice, score, noul — is answered by one forward pass. See it triage an inbox, play a game one decision at a time, and run the smallest round. No generated tokens.
pages.social_description: One state, a tree of typed questions, one forward pass, typed answers. Snake, Pac-Man, an inbox, and the smallest round — with the model's own probabilities.
pages.twitter_description: One state, a tree of typed questions, one forward pass, typed answers.

pages.title: emb — demos: the model lens — two models, two spaces
pages.description: The same corpus, the same query, two embedding models. The rankings differ, the projections differ, and neither one is wrong: vectors from two models are not comparable.
pages.social_description: One corpus under two models: the same query returns different neighbours, because each model defines its own space.

pages.title: emb — demos: the medium — identify the tune, describe the music and the footage
pages.description: A Shazam-style fingerprint names the exact recording from a noisy four-second excerpt, computed live in the browser. Beside it, real models answer the semantic question: CLAP retrieves music by a phrase, and X-CLIP retrieves footage by a phrase, both over an index built offline and queried live.
pages.social_title: emb — demos: the medium — name the tune, find the moment
pages.social_description: A fingerprint names the exact recording; an embedding says what kind of thing it is. Then a clip is searched frame by frame by a phrase.
pages.twitter_description: A fingerprint names the exact recording; an embedding says what kind of thing it is.

pages.title: emb — demos: the languages — one space for six of them
pages.description: One sentence and its translations in five languages, each compared with the English original by a multilingual model in the sandbox. No translator runs; the model reads every language itself.
pages.social_description: A multilingual model puts translations and unrelated sentences in one space; the plate shows which ones land together.

pages.title: emb — demos: the search — a question answered by meaning
pages.description: A query phrased in words the corpus never contains, answered with the passages that mean it: an exact vector search over a committed index, reranked by the sandbox's own Lua.
pages.social_description: Retrieval by meaning: one query embedded live, thousands of passages searched in the browser, and the result reranked by the server.

pages.title: emb — demos: the similarity — one number between two texts
pages.description: Two passages through the sandbox's own preloaded Lua preset: the dimension, the norm, and the cosine similarity, with the script's source and digest beside the reply.
pages.social_description: Similarity as a single number, computed by the server's own script and shown with the script's bytes.

pages.title: emb — demos: the vector — text becomes 384 numbers
pages.description: Watch a sentence become an embedding: the dimension, the L2 norm and the bytes of the vector a real model returned, from a real server.
pages.social_description: One passage through a real embeddings server, showing the vector itself: dimension, norm and bytes.

pages.title: emb — documentation: install, commands, replies, Lua
pages.description: Reference for emb, a simple yet powerful self-hosted inference server that speaks the Redis protocol: install, commands, reply formats, configuration, Lua scripting, operations and benchmarks.
pages.social_description: Reference for emb, a simple yet powerful self-hosted inference server that speaks the Redis protocol: install, commands, reply formats, configuration, Lua scripting, operations and benchmarks.
pages.twitter_description: The hosted reference for emb: install, commands, reply formats, configuration, Lua scripting, operations and benchmarks.

pages.title: emb — the Ruby client: one call, one command, and the shape of your call site
pages.description: How the emb Ruby gem turns a call site into one EMB or one EMB.MULTI: the four wire shapes, the create-then-consume rule, fail-closed batches, and the emb-server gem that ships the server as a precompiled binary.
pages.social_description: Four execution modes, four wire shapes, and the one rule that decides how many commands a scope costs.

pages.title: emb — a fast embedding server that speaks the Redis protocol
pages.description: emb is a simple yet powerful inference server that speaks the Redis protocol. ONNX Runtime inference, smart batching, LRU cache, multi-model queries.
pages.social_description: A fast embedding server that speaks the Redis protocol. ONNX Runtime inference, smart batching, LRU cache.
pages.twitter_description: A fast embedding server that speaks the Redis protocol.

pages.title: emb — scripting: the Lua host API, sandbox, budgets, reply grammar
pages.description: Reference for emb's scripting engine: EMB.EVAL, EMB.EVSHA and EMB.SCRIPT, the sandbox, the complete emb.* host API, tensor specs, the Lua-to-RESP reply grammar, evaluation budgets and reply-cache identity.
pages.social_description: Reference for emb's scripting engine: EMB.EVAL, EMB.EVSHA and EMB.SCRIPT, the sandbox, the complete emb.* host API, tensor specs, the reply grammar, budgets and cache identity.
pages.twitter_description: The complete scripting reference for emb: commands, sandbox, host API, tensors, replies, budgets and cache identity.
